newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks close slightly off on dollar woes.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks close slightly off on dollar woes.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks clawed back most of their morning losses but still ended a hair down on Thursday on worries over U.S.interest rates and the weakness of U.S. dollar, brokers said.
The Hang Seng Index closed down 7.35 points at 11,586.68. Turnover was HK$4.81 billion, a hefty drop from Wednesday's HK$6.07 billion.
"People were a little nervous today about the dollar," said Angus Shillington of Asia Equity. "The trade report affected the dollar which in turn hit the equity markets."
The U.S. Commerce Department announced on Wednesday the U.S. trade deficit increased 42.6 percent in July, widening to US$11.68 billion from June's US$8.9 billion.
In New York, the U.S. dollar temporarily fell below 109 yen on the news, recovering to 109.34 yen by late Asian trade.
Market sentiment in Hong Kong remains optimistic if not all that active, brokers said.
"Investors are bullish on Hong Kong but on the sidelines today," said a broker with a Singaporean house.
Overseas investors are prepared to increase their weighting in Hong Kong once the U.S. uncertainty is eliminated, she added.
"Market leader HSBC was well supported even though the market fell 60 points early in the day," noted K.L. Wong, institutional sales manager at Kerry Securities.
The finance sector led the market, rising 0.68 percent compared with a 0.06 percent decline for the Hang Seng Index.
Banking giant HSBC gained HK$1.50 to close at HK$140.50 on moderate volume of 1.43 million shares worth HK$199.91 million. The share is still trading at a large discount to the market, brokers said.
In the utility sector, China Light continued its strong advance, rising HK$0.40 to HK$35.40.
Buying interest in conglomerate Wheelock was strong. The share rose HK$0.45 to HK$17.05. Brokers could cite no reason for the share's strength.
Properties came in for profit-taking, particularly market leader Henderson Land, which shed HK$0.50 to HK$64.00.
Sun Hung Kai Properties also lost HK$0.50 to HK$78.50, and Cheung Kong fell HK$0.50 to HK$56.75.
